Perfect alignment on AMD drug enrichment findings (C61-C64). Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. Neither raises concerns about the drug predictions or the arsenous acid negative control.

Perfect alignment on MS pathway enrichment (C73-C76). Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes proper FDR correction, while peer reviewers accept the connections to known MS biology.

Perfect alignment on omnigenic root causal model (C21-C23, C83-C91). Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes empirical validation from both diseases, while Reviewer 2 notes 'solid theoretical background.'
Perfect alignment on unknown confounding limitation (C99). Both evaluations find this SUPPORTED as an honest acknowledgment of a standard limitation in observational causal inference.

Divergent evaluations on DAG assumption (C100-C101). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED, noting empirical robustness to cycles. Peer Reviewer 1 rates UNCERTAIN, calling it 'an important weakness' and providing IL2 feedback loop example, though acknowledging simulation evidence of robustness. Editor notes 'strong assumptions' but 'solid empirical evidence' of robustness to violations.

Perfect alignment on main conclusion (C102). Both evaluations find this claim SUPPORTED. OpenEval traces support through multiple lines of evidence, while peer reviewers affirm novelty, importance, and successful problem-solving. Reviewer 2 states 'authors addressed all of my comments.'

Alignment on RNA-seq measurement error handling (C3, C34-C36). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with detailed analysis of mathematical derivation and asymptotic arguments. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these technical choices without challenge, as indicated by editor's statement about 'solid empirical evidence.'

Divergent evaluations on cross-context transfer (C4, C5, C20, C37-C38). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED, emphasizing robustness validation in Appendix. Peer Reviewer 1 rates UNCERTAIN, questioning whether K562 leukemia cells are suitable for learning regulatory structure of MS CD4+ cells, suggesting RCSP should model uncertainty in structure transfer despite acknowledging Supplementary Figure 4 robustness analysis.

Alignment on AMD validation with age as root cause (C47-C50). Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes this as important positive control with known ground truth, while peer reviewers accept AMD findings without challenge.

Divergent evaluations on novelty claims (C2, C16-C19). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting strong assertions about field state with limited citations and difficulty verifying 'no existing algorithms' claim without comprehensive literature review. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, with all three reviewers affirming novelty and importance of the framework.

Alignment on RCS mathematical properties (C27-C31, C92-C94). Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes formal definitions and internal consistency, while Reviewer 2 notes 'solid theoretical background.'

Alignment on MS patient clustering and drug sensitivity (C77-C79). Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes proper multiple testing correction and clinical relevance, while peer reviewers accept these findings as part of MS analysis.

Alignment on MS subtype validation (C80-C82). Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes validation through matching known disease subtypes, while peer reviewers accept the biological validation.

Alignment on bulk RNA-seq limitation (C95-C96). Both evaluations find this SUPPORTED as honest limitation acknowledgment. OpenEval notes this follows from bulk RNA-seq choice, while peer reviewers accept this limitation without challenge.

Alignment on Perturb-seq technology limitation (C97-C98). Both evaluations find this SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes limitation is inherent to available data, while Reviewer 1 explicitly addresses this, noting TFs may not be expressed highly enough for detection and suggesting modified language about RCSP capabilities.

Alignment on RCS metric limitation regarding effect direction (C92-C94). Both evaluations find this SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes empirical validation that signed RCS approximates root causal effect well, while peer reviewers accept the mathematical properties without challenge.

Alignment on distribution of root causal vs correlated genes (C51-C52). Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes consistency with omnigenic hypothesis and evidence that RCS distinguishes root causality from correlation, while peer reviewers accept AMD findings including these distributional results.
